I'll think through this as the farmer, then give you the plan.

---

**My thinking for this year:**

I've been doing cabbage-eggplant on this 4.5 mu ground for many years now. It works well — cabbage comes off in late spring, then I put eggplant in right after and it runs through summer into autumn. Two crops off the same ground, that's how I make this small piece of land earn enough for me and my wife.

For cabbage, I always plant the hybrid seed — the one the seed dealer in town sells, I think "Zhonggan 11" type. The old varieties don't head up tight and buyers don't want them. I transplant seedlings around late February under small film tunnel, harvest by middle of May. Before planting I spread about 3 carts of chicken manure across the whole plot, then I rotary till it in deep. On top of that I put about 50 kg of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base. After the plants take hold, I topdress urea twice — maybe 15 kg per mu each time, once when the outer leaves spread and once when the head starts to form. I know some neighbors put less, but I'd rather spend the extra 30-40 yuan per mu than see loose heads that only sell for half price. I water maybe 5 times — after transplant, then every 10-12 days in the dry spring. Cabbage gets aphids and cabbage worm, I spray 4 times, nothing too expensive.

Eggplant is more work and takes more fertilizer, especially potash — if potash is short the fruits come out small and the color dull. I buy grafted seedlings from the market, they resist bacterial wilt better. I transplant end of May after cabbage comes off, no need to plough again deep, just rotary till and form ridges. Base fertilizer another 3 carts manure plus 60 kg compound per mu. Then through the summer I topdress urea and potash sulfate maybe 3 times, totaling around 25 kg N and 25 kg K on top. Eggplant drinks water — I irrigate every 7-8 days when it's fruiting, probably 10 times total from the well. Pests are heavy in summer: whitefly, red spider, 28-spotted beetle, fruit borer — I spray about 8 times, rotating chemicals so the bugs don't get used to them.

Quzhou soil here is decent loam, not too salty, the well water is fine. My main worry is always prices at harvest — if cabbage price drops I still have to sell it. That's why I don't plant all 4.5 mu to one thing, and why the eggplant crop matters — summer vegetable prices hold up better.
